nodes.validation: Out-of-sample substrates and enzyme mutants

nodes.validation: ML-guided identification of high-yield conditions in expanded chemical space

nodes.data_regime: >240,000 crystallized mononuclear TMCs
nodes.validation: Analysis of coordination, metal and donor-space undersampling

nodes.validation: Predicts unseen low-symmetry complex and model catalytic reaction energies
nodes.why: A physically structured alternative to black-box learning that explicitly models ligand-ligand interactions.

nodes.validation: Cross-species, cross-computational-setup and computation-to-experiment transfer
nodes.why: Useful conceptual reference for reusable latent representations and extreme few-shot transfer, even though demonstrated on heterogeneous catalysis.

nodes.validation: Maintained conversion/selectivity while reducing reaction time and Rh loading by 10-30x

nodes.label: Catalysing (Organo-)Catalysis: ML Trends in Enantioselective Organocatalysis
nodes.chemistry: Enantioselective organocatalysis
nodes.data_regime: Review of historical and recent ML applications in organocatalysis
nodes.validation: N/A
nodes.why: Adds the organocatalysis branch, often omitted when ML-in-catalysis discussions focus only on transition metals.

nodes.label: Multidimensional Steric Parameters in Asymmetric Catalysis
nodes.chemistry: Asymmetric catalysis; directional Sterimol parameterization of substituents
nodes.data_regime: Small published enantioselectivity series
nodes.validation: Retrospective correlation with selectivity; steric terms interpreted mechanistically
nodes.why: Moved Sterimol from QSAR into homogeneous catalysis: L, B1 and B5 report where bulk sits, not only a cone angle.
nodes.summary: Sigman lab showed that Verloop Sterimol parameters, used as a chemist-defined steric frame, can give compact multivariable models of enantioselectivity. Direct ancestor of DescriPyTor’s orientational Sterimol terms.

nodes.label: Interrogating Selectivity in Catalysis Using Molecular Vibrations
nodes.chemistry: Asymmetric catalysis; IR vibrations as electronic descriptors
nodes.data_regime: Small catalytic selectivity datasets
nodes.validation: Interpretable vibrational terms mapped onto the selectivity-determining interaction
nodes.why: Milo/Sigman prototype for reading an electronic descriptor from a chemically chosen site rather than a generic molecular fingerprint.
nodes.summary: Uses IR stretching frequencies as site-anchored electronic descriptors in multivariable models of catalytic selectivity. The same premise — choose where to read the feature — is the DescriPyTor reference-frame argument.

nodes.label: A Data-Intensive Approach to Mechanistic Elucidation in Chiral Anion Catalysis
nodes.chemistry: Chiral anion organocatalysis; catalyst–substrate parameterization
nodes.data_regime: Designed small catalytic library, not a large HTE dump
nodes.validation: Statistical models used to distinguish competing mechanistic hypotheses
nodes.why: Canonical Milo-lab result: a small, chemically designed dataset plus interpretable descriptors can interrogate mechanism.
nodes.summary: Parameterizes catalysts and substrates in a chiral-anion system and uses the fitted models to distinguish mechanisms. Template for DescriPyTor’s claim that small catalytic sets need chemist-guided features, not bigger descriptor pools.

nodes.label: A Modern Approach to Steric Effects in Hammett-Type Correlations
nodes.chemistry: Physical-organic catalysis; steric correction of Hammett-type models
nodes.data_regime: Classic linear free-energy series plus Sterimol terms
nodes.validation: Improved correlations when steric and electronic terms are separated geometrically
nodes.why: Puts Sterimol on the same footing as σ constants — the electronic/steric split DescriPyTor still uses.
nodes.summary: Shows that Sterimol steric terms can be combined with Hammett electronic parameters instead of burying steric demand in a single substituent constant. Milo is a coauthor; this is the closest published ancestor of chemist-guided steric frames.

nodes.label: Predictive and Mechanistic Multivariate Linear Regression for Reaction Development
nodes.chemistry: Asymmetric catalysis; MLR workflow for selectivity models
nodes.data_regime: Review of small-to-moderate catalytic modeling case studies
nodes.validation: N/A
nodes.why: The playbook DescriPyTor still follows: exhaustively search a chemist-designed descriptor pool, then validate on Q² not R².
nodes.summary: Sigman-group tutorial on multivariate linear regression for reaction development: how to choose physical-organic descriptors, avoid overfitting, and read mechanism from the selected terms. Direct methodological backdrop for DescriPyTor’s modeling stage.

nodes.label: Conformational Effects on Sterimol Steric Parameters
nodes.chemistry: Asymmetric catalysis; conformer-averaged Sterimol descriptors
nodes.data_regime: Catalytic case studies where a single conformer misrepresents steric demand
nodes.validation: Boltzmann-weighted Sterimol outperforms single-conformer values
nodes.why: Shows that the geometry a steric descriptor is read from is itself a modeling variable — the same point DescriPyTor makes for metal complexes vs free ligands.
nodes.summary: Paton lab: Sterimol values change with conformation, and Boltzmann averaging is required before the descriptor is used in a selectivity model. DescriPyTor’s case studies treat structure choice (product, free ligand, metal complex) as the analogous decision.

nodes.label: Auto-QChem: Automated DFT Descriptor Workflows for Organic Molecules
nodes.chemistry: Organic molecules including catalytic ligands and substrates; automated DFT featurization
nodes.data_regime: Reusable DFT descriptor database generated from SMILES inputs
nodes.validation: Workflow benchmarks and downstream modeling use-cases
nodes.why: The Doyle-lab pipeline DescriPyTor contrasts with: compute a large fixed descriptor pool, then model. No user-defined chemical axes.
nodes.summary: Automates DFT jobs and stores molecular descriptors from SMILES. Important platform paper: it solves extraction, not reference-frame choice. DescriPyTor’s claim is that in small catalytic sets the missing control is where each descriptor is read.

nodes.label: Mechanistic Inference from Statistical Models at Different Data-Size Regimes
nodes.chemistry: Homogeneous catalysis; how dataset size changes what a statistical model can claim
nodes.data_regime: Explicit comparison across small vs larger catalytic data-size regimes
nodes.validation: Shows when fitted equations support mechanistic claims versus when they only interpolate
nodes.why: Milo-lab warning that DescriPyTor is built on: with n in the tens, an unconstrained descriptor search will overfit.
nodes.summary: Maps what statistical models in catalysis can and cannot support as n grows. The small-n regime is exactly where DescriPyTor insists on a chemist-chosen reference frame instead of a free search over hundreds of features.

nodes.label: AQME: Automated Quantum Mechanical Environments for Descriptor Generation
nodes.chemistry: General molecular / catalysis descriptor generation from automated quantum chemistry
nodes.data_regime: Broad descriptor pools assembled per molecule from QM and steric codes
nodes.validation: Software demonstration and downstream modeling examples
nodes.why: The Paton/Alegre-Requena platform DescriPyTor is written against: Sterimol and %Vbur from supplied geometries, not user-defined axes.
nodes.summary: End-to-end automated QM environment that computes charges, frequencies, Sterimol and buried volume. DescriPyTor keeps this broad pool, then adds chemist-chosen axes for orientational Sterimol and projected dipoles.

nodes.label: Small Data Can Play a Big Role in Chemical Discovery
nodes.chemistry: Chemical discovery including catalysis; advocacy for small, designed datasets
nodes.data_regime: n/a overview
nodes.validation: N/A
nodes.why: Milo-lab manifesto for the DescriPyTor setting: do not wait for HTE-scale data if the representation is chemically right.
nodes.summary: Argues that carefully designed small datasets, paired with interpretable representations, can drive discovery. Sets the lab stance that DescriPyTor operationalizes: descriptor frame first, more data second.

nodes.label: ROBERT: Automated Machine Learning for Chemistry
nodes.chemistry: Chemistry ML including homogeneous catalysis; automated model screening from feature matrices
nodes.data_regime: Designed for the small-n chemical tables AQME and similar tools export
nodes.validation: Automated model comparison with reported diagnostics
nodes.why: DescriPyTor exports its labeled feature matrices here. ROBERT screens models; it does not choose the chemical reference frame.
nodes.summary: Bridges chemistry descriptor tables to automated model selection. Complementary to DescriPyTor: once the chemist has anchored Sterimol and dipole columns to atoms and axes, ROBERT can hunt the equation.

nodes.label: SMARTpy: Cavity Steric Molecular Descriptors
nodes.chemistry: Homogeneous catalysis; cavity-specific steric descriptors beyond classical Sterimol
nodes.data_regime: Applied to diverse catalytic and molecular systems
nodes.validation: Case studies against established steric parameterizations
nodes.why: Newest Sigman-lab steric software: measures bulk in a cavity, not only along a substituent axis. Natural comparison for DescriPyTor’s orientational Sterimol.
nodes.summary: Python package for cavity-centric steric descriptors. Like morfeus and DBSTEP, it computes steric numbers from a supplied geometry; unlike DescriPyTor, the chemist does not define an orientational reference frame on the substituent axis.

nodes.label: ChemRefine: Automated Interoperable ML and Quantum Chemistry Platform
nodes.journal: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
nodes.chemistry: General molecular / organometallic simulation; automated QM and ML interoperability
nodes.data_regime: Workflow platform rather than a single catalytic dataset
nodes.validation: Software interoperability demonstrations across QM and ML engines
nodes.why: 2026 platform in the same automation layer as AQME/Auto-QChem. DescriPyTor cites it as adjacent infrastructure, not a chemist-guided frame.
nodes.summary: Open platform that chains quantum chemistry and machine-learning simulations. Relevant because DescriPyTor is a lighter, chemist-in-the-loop alternative: it does not try to own the full simulation stack, only the reference frame of each descriptor.

nodes.label: CREST: Exploration of Low-Energy Molecular Chemical Space
nodes.chemistry: Ground-state conformational ensembles for molecules and complexes; not a TS-ensemble generator
nodes.data_regime: Software paper; computational examples across drug-sized molecules
nodes.validation: Benchmarked conformational coverage and timings versus earlier CREST/xTB workflows
nodes.why: Canonical ground-state conformer tool. Distinct from racerTS: CREST samples minima (and can constrain TSs only at extra cost), not TS ensembles by default.
nodes.summary: CREST is the workhorse for low-energy conformer–rotamer ensembles at GFN-xTB/GFN-FF cost. In a catalysis stack it belongs in the ground-state layer. Do not treat it as interchangeable with racerTS, which samples transition-state conformers.

nodes.label: autodE: Automated Calculation of Reaction Energy Profiles
nodes.chemistry: Automated reaction-profile search for molecular and transition-metal reactions from SMILES-level input
nodes.data_regime: Computational benchmarks on organic and organometallic reactions
nodes.validation: Recovered literature TSs and reaction energies across a curated reaction set
nodes.why: TS localization from a reaction string — the search step before ensemble sampling or descriptors. TS-tools sits on top of this layer.
nodes.summary: autodE automates locating TSs and assembling reaction energy profiles for organic and organometallic chemistry. It is a TS-search tool, not a conformer sampler and not a supervised ML model.

nodes.label: TS-tools: Automated TS Localization from Reaction SMILES
nodes.chemistry: Automated TS searches including multi-molecular and solvent-sensitive pathways
nodes.data_regime: Benchmark set of mono-, bi-, and multimolecular reactions
nodes.validation: 95% success already at xTB for mono/bimolecular TSs; DFT required more often for multimolecular paths
nodes.why: Faster TS guesses from reaction SMILES. Complements autodE; still not a TS-conformer ensemble tool.
nodes.summary: TS-tools locates transition states from textual reaction SMILES at xTB or DFT. High success on simple reactions; harder multi-molecular and solvent-switched mechanisms need DFT. Use it for TS search, then racerTS if you need a TS ensemble.

nodes.label: racerTS: Rapid Transition-State Conformer Ensembles
nodes.chemistry: TS conformer ensembles for 20 diverse reactions, including catalysis-relevant TSs
nodes.data_regime: Computational benchmark: 20 reaction TSs versus CREST and GOAT
nodes.validation: Similar coverage to CREST, better DFT-optimized TS validity, median 0.17 kcal/mol low-energy error, far lower wall time
nodes.why: This is the TS-ensemble layer. CREST/GOAT are expensive stand-ins; racerTS is built to sample TS conformers, not ground-state minima.
nodes.summary: racerTS generates TS conformer ensembles with constrained distance geometry. It is not CREST: CREST explores ground-state chemical space; racerTS freezes the reaction center and samples the rest. Needed before TS-informed descriptors or MLIP datasets.

nodes.label: GoodVibes: Automated Quasi-Harmonic Thermochemistry
nodes.chemistry: Thermochemical corrections from Gaussian/ORCA/xTB frequency jobs used throughout homogeneous catalysis DFT
nodes.data_regime: Software paper with worked catalytic reaction-path examples
nodes.validation: Reproducible quasi-harmonic G values versus raw RRHO; community standard in Paton/Alegre-Requena workflows
nodes.why: After a TS or minimum is found, free energies still need quasi-harmonic treatment. This is the thermochemistry layer, not a model.
nodes.summary: GoodVibes applies Grimme/Truhlar quasi-harmonic corrections and frequency scaling to electronic-structure outputs. In the stack it sits after conformer/TS optimization and before descriptors or ΔG-based ranking. AQME/ROBERT often assume this step exists.

nodes.label: thermoMLIP: MLIP-Enhanced Thermochemistry
nodes.chemistry: Organic thermochemistry across chemical space; relevant when catalysis models need cheap, consistent ΔG
nodes.data_regime: Computational organic chemical space plus an actively learned thermodynamic dataset
nodes.validation: Near-DFT thermochemistry; MLIP conformer searches often find lower-energy structures than existing datasets
nodes.why: MLIP replacement for the expensive DFT thermochemistry layer. Complements GoodVibes rather than replacing quasi-harmonic logic.
nodes.summary: thermoMLIP uses MLIPs to optimize conformers and evaluate thermochemistry near DFT quality, then trains a fast GNN surrogate. Use it when the bottleneck is ΔG at scale, not when you need a TS ensemble (that is racerTS) or experiment selection (that is EDBO).

nodes.label: EDBO: Bayesian Reaction Optimization for Chemical Synthesis
nodes.chemistry: Pd-catalyzed direct arylation benchmark plus Mitsunobu and deoxyfluorination case studies
nodes.data_regime: Large Pd arylation HTE benchmark plus closed-loop synthetic case studies versus expert chemists
nodes.validation: Prospective comparison with expert human experiment selection; BO more efficient and more consistent
nodes.why: EDBO chooses the next experiment. It is not a supervised yield model and not a descriptor engine.
nodes.summary: Introduces Experimental Design via Bayesian Optimization (EDBO) and shows it can beat expert chemists at picking the next reaction conditions. Type this as experiment selection / BO, not as supervised ML on a static dataset.

nodes.label: EDBO+: Multi-Objective Active Learning for Reaction Optimization
nodes.chemistry: Ni/photoredox enantioselective cross-electrophile coupling as a real multi-objective test case
nodes.data_regime: HTE and virtual-screening datasets plus a live Ni photoredox optimization campaign
nodes.validation: Prospective multi-objective laboratory optimization; web app removes a coding barrier
nodes.why: EDBO+ is still experiment selection, now Pareto-aware. Do not collapse it into the Ni 2024 application paper or into supervised regression.
nodes.summary: EDBO+ extends EDBO to multiple objectives (yield vs selectivity vs cost) with a chemist-facing web app. Same stack layer as EDBO: choose the next experiment. The later Sigman/Doyle Ni reduction paper uses EDBO+; this is the method paper.

nodes.label: molli: Combinatorial Libraries and Feature Extraction
nodes.chemistry: General molecular / homogeneous-ligand libraries; combinatorial feature extraction, not a catalytic reference frame
nodes.data_regime: Software paper; combinatorial molecular libraries rather than a single catalytic n
nodes.validation: Software demonstration across library generation and feature-extraction workflows
nodes.why: Denmark-lab infrastructure for making libraries and extracting features. Contrast for DescriPyTor: no chemist-chosen substituent axis.
nodes.summary: Python toolkit for combinatorial small-molecule libraries and feature extraction. Useful when the bottleneck is enumerating molecules. DescriPyTor’s claim is different: on small catalytic n the missing control is where each descriptor is read, not another feature extractor.

nodes.label: SambVca 2: Topographic Steric Maps of Catalytic Pockets
nodes.chemistry: Homogeneous catalysis; metal-centered steric maps for NHCs, phosphines, and catalytic pockets
nodes.data_regime: Software paper with organometallic pocket examples
nodes.validation: Web-tool demonstration of topographic maps versus classical %Vbur numbers
nodes.why: Canonical cavity/pocket steric software. The frame is a metal-centered sphere, not a chemist-oriented substituent axis.
nodes.summary: SambVca 2 turns buried volume into topographic steric maps of the catalytic pocket. Same steric family as %Vbur and SMARTpy; opposite origin of the frame from DescriPyTor’s orientational Sterimol.

nodes.label: Online Computer-Aided Design of Catalytic Pockets
nodes.chemistry: Homogeneous catalysis; online design of catalytic pockets from buried-volume maps
nodes.data_regime: Computational pocket-design case studies across organometallic catalysts
nodes.validation: Case studies connecting pocket topography to known catalytic behavior
nodes.why: The high-profile cavity paper: design the pocket, not a substituent axis. Natural contrast for DescriPyTor’s orientational Sterimol.
nodes.summary: Shows how topographic steric maps can be used to design catalytic pockets online. Measures cavity occupancy around a metal; DescriPyTor instead lets the chemist point the steric frame along a chosen substituent.

nodes.label: Percent Buried Volume for Phosphines and NHCs
nodes.chemistry: Homogeneous catalysis; %Vbur as a steric number for phosphines and NHCs
nodes.data_regime: Method paper; computational buried-volume examples on common ligands
nodes.validation: Comparisons of %Vbur with Tolman cone angle and related steric scales
nodes.why: The single-number buried-volume ancestor. Metal-centered sphere, no user-defined substituent axis.
nodes.summary: Defines percent buried volume as a practical steric parameter for phosphines and NHCs. AQME, SambVca and SMARTpy all sit downstream of this number. DescriPyTor’s steric terms are directional Sterimol, not a metal-centered occupancy.

nodes.label: Multidimensional Analysis Tools for Asymmetric Catalysis
nodes.chemistry: Asymmetric catalysis; the Sigman/Milo playbook for chemist-designed descriptors and MLR
nodes.data_regime: n/a overview of multivariable catalytic modeling case studies
nodes.validation: N/A
nodes.why: The written playbook DescriPyTor still follows: chemist-designed descriptors, then MLR. Milo is a coauthor.
nodes.summary: Accounts of how multidimensional analysis — Sterimol, IR, Hammett-type terms, MLR — became a catalytic workflow. Direct ancestor of DescriPyTor’s modeling stage; it does not yet require a user-defined orientational reference frame.

nodes.label: Ligand Knowledge Base for Phosphorus Donor Ligands
nodes.chemistry: Homogeneous catalysis; reaction-agnostic DFT maps of phosphorus-donor ligand space
nodes.data_regime: Computational phosphine ligand maps rather than a single catalytic dataset
nodes.validation: PCA maps of ligand space compared with known organometallic trends
nodes.why: The original reaction-agnostic ligand library. Kraken is the scaled descendant; DescriPyTor argues the opposite direction.
nodes.summary: Builds a DFT descriptor knowledge base for phosphorus donor ligands and maps ligand space. This is the library alternative: precomputed, reaction-agnostic features. DescriPyTor instead reads descriptors from a chemist-chosen frame on a small catalytic n.

nodes.label: Computational Ligand Descriptors for Catalyst Design
nodes.chemistry: Homogeneous catalysis; survey of computational ligand descriptors used in catalyst design
nodes.data_regime: n/a overview of computational ligand-descriptor methods
nodes.validation: N/A
nodes.why: The map of the library/descriptor landscape DescriPyTor is written against: computational ligand space rather than chemist-chosen axes.
nodes.summary: Reviews computational ligand descriptors for catalyst design, from knowledge bases to steric maps. Use it as the landscape paper: most of the field precomputes ligand space; DescriPyTor asks the chemist to define the frame on the reaction at hand.
